problem: Find $(2a+3c)\times (b+2c)$, if $a\times b=3i-2j+k$, $a\times c=j-2k$ and $b\times c=2i-3j.$

feedback.problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 7 & -17\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 7 & -17\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $AC=CA={I}_{3}$
- $AD=DA={I}_{3}$
- $D={A}^{-1}$
feedback.worked_solution:
- First, we check whether $AC=CA={I}_{3}.$ Computing $AC$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 7 & -17\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, computing $CA$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}CA & =\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 7 & -17\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, statement I is true.

- Now, we check whether $AD=DA={I}_{3}.$ Computing $AD$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AD & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -4 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -1 & 7 & -17\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & 7 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne {I}_{3}.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, statement II is false. As a result, $D\ne {A}^{-1}$ and statement III is false too.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

feedback.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $A(1,1,0)$ and $B(3,-1,2).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $A$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=a+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $a$ is the position vector of $A.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $A(1,1,0)$ and $B(3,-1,2)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{AB} \\  & =⟨3,-1,2⟩-⟨1,1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-2,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
